tool_input.command: for f in src/features/comments/components/*.tsx; do echo "==== $f"; cat "$f"; done; echo; echo "==== authorization"; ls src/lib; cat src/lib/authorization.tsx 2>/dev/null || cat src/lib/authorization.ts
tool_input.description: Show comment components and authorization lib

result:
Authors can now edit their own comments from the comments list, with a drawer and a "Comment Updated" success notification. I did not run tests, lint, type checks or the app, as you asked, so none of this has been verified beyond reading it.

What changed in `apps/react-vite`:

- **API** (`src/features/comments/api/update-comment.ts`): `updateComment` sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` with `{ body }`. `useUpdateComment` refetches the discussion's comments and shows the success notification in `onSuccess`, as the project rules require.
- **Mock API** (`src/testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts`): a new PATCH handler. It returns 404 for an unknown comment, 403 when the caller is not the author, and otherwise saves the body and returns the comment with its author.
- **Policy** (`src/lib/authorization.tsx`): `POLICIES['comment:edit']` is true only when the comment's author is the current user. Admins do not get Edit on other people's comments, because the roles table does not give admins that right.
- **UI** (`src/features/comments/components/update-comment.tsx`, wired into `comments-list.tsx`): an Edit button that opens a form drawer prefilled with the comment body. It sits beside Delete and is hidden unless the policy passes.
- **Test** (`src/app/routes/app/discussions/__tests__/discussion.test.tsx`): one new journey test. It checks that the author sees Edit, saves a change, and sees the success message, and that a teammate's comment has no Edit button. It has not been run.

Things to know:

- The existing discussion and comment components call `useNotifications` inside the component. I put the notification in the hook instead, because the project rules say so. I did not touch the older code.
- The existing delete check wraps the whole header row (date and author), so a regular user sees no header on other people's comments. I left that as it was.

I have not committed anything.
